holidays.name: National Cheese Lovers Day
holidays.description: Grab a cracker and get ready to celebrate. This day is for anyone who thinks the cheese board is the best part of the party. Sharp cheddar, stinky blue and gooey brie all count. Melted or not, it's all welcome.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday. It appears to have started as a grassroots celebration among cheese fans and food marketers, and its exact origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: It takes about 10 pounds of milk to make just 1 pound of cheese. A single wedge represents a lot of cows' work.

holidays.name: National Penguin Day
holidays.description: Break out your best tuxedo and waddle with pride. This day celebrates the tuxedoed birds of the southern seas. It's a chance to appreciate their huddling and sliding, and their devotion as parents.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is popular with zoos, aquariums and wildlife fans, who use it to spotlight penguin conservation.
holidays.funFact: Male emperor penguins keep their eggs warm on their feet through the Antarctic winter. Some go without eating for more than two months while they do it.

holidays.name: National Buttercrunch Day
holidays.description: This is a salute to the buttery, crackly toffee candy, usually coated in chocolate and rolled in crushed nuts. It's a good excuse to snap off a piece, and to pretend your dentist isn't watching.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It was likely created to honor the classic confection that has long filled holiday candy tins.
holidays.funFact: Buttercrunch is a type of toffee. Toffee is made by cooking sugar and butter to the "hard crack" stage, around 300°F, which is what gives it its snap.
